newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Pepsi sees slow but steady Venezuela return.
newsitem.headline: Pepsi sees slow but steady Venezuela return.

text.p: Soft drinks giant PepsiCo will regain its footing in the Venezuelan market slowly but steadily, Pepsi Chief Executive Roger Enrico said Monday.

Pepsi formerly dominated the Venezuelan soft drinks market. But after the suprise switch of the country's leading bottler, Grupo Cisneros Embotelladoras de Venezuela, to Coca-Cola Co. in August, Pepsi products virtually disappeared from Venezuela, where it once had an 80 percent share.
"It's going to take us a good two years to get back to where we were," Enrico told reporters. "But let me tell you, this will not be a 100-yard dash ... we're here for a long time".

Pepsi, which signed a 30/70 joint venture deal with leading Venezuelan foods and beverage company Polar in November to bottle and distribute cola, expects sales to recover to 50 million cases by mid-1997 in a market estimated at 200 million cases a year.
Enrico also said PepsiCo had sold worldwide 1,000 company-owned restaurants to franchisees over the past year and a half and that it would continue that policy as franchisees were more efficient.
Separately, Argentina's Buenos Aires Embotelladora SA (BAESA), the biggest Pepsi bottler outside the United States, said Monday it lost $426.4 million in the year to Sept. 30.
Results include an extraordinary loss of $126.3 million, BAESA told the Buenos Aires Stock Exchange.
From July 1 Pepsi took over operating control of BAESA, which has suffered a financial crunch that many analysts blame on overexpansion.
In September shareholders of BAESA filed a class action suit in Manhattan federal court against both BAESA and Pepsi alleging they hid the bottler's problems.
PepsiCo's stock rose 25 cents to $29.625 on the New York Stock Exchange.
